documentation.rationale: The identity half is partly present: VIN photographed, year/trim consistent, equipment list, and a clean title claimed but not shown. The maintenance half is absent: no receipts, no history report, no photos of the rear subframe.

condition.rationale: Photos show a tidy interior with intact two-tone leather, an intact top with a clear glass rear window, a clean engine bay and a dry-looking front/mid underside. Cooling, VANOS and rear structure are unproven. The steering wheel cover hides the rim condition.

price_value.rationale: At $15,250 the ask sits just above the $11,754–$14,977 fair-value range (mid $13,355), with no records to justify a premium. The car has been listed about a year at the same price, which suggests room to negotiate.

mission_fit.rationale: This is a factory manual M54 3.0i within the ideal budget band, which is the core bridge candidate. Undocumented cooling and rear-structure history keep it at a plausible fit rather than a decisive one.

logistics.rationale: The car is in Columbia, SC, far from Carmel, with PPI access unstated and a private seller. The independent BMW shops in the Columbia area could do a PPI if the seller agrees. CA registration should be feasible but needs a smog test and VIN verification.

emotional_spec_fit.rationale: Grey over black/red two-tone sport seats, a manual with a claimed LSD, cross-spoke sport wheels, an M wheel and roll hoops make an attractive spec. The aftermarket strut brace, wheel cover and possible aftermarket radiator are minor deviations from stock.

ppi_focus: Rear subframe mounts and trunk-floor spot welds (especially the left side) plus the differential mount ears, checked from below and inside the trunk
Cooling system: radiator brand and fitment, water pump play, expansion tank and bleeder, hoses, and a pressure test
Engine scan for stored codes; VANOS rattle and DISA valve check on cold start
Oil filter housing gasket, valve cover gasket and rear main seal for leaks
Rear trailing-arm bushings and front control-arm bushings
Clutch engagement point and slip test; shifter bushings; confirm the LSD is present
Convertible top frame, latches, rear glass bonding and drain channels; window regulators
Tire date codes and wear pattern
Rocker, floor and subframe-mount rust (humid Southeast car)
Dash top for cracks, and the cluster for pixel fade
what_would_change_verdict: Up: a clean specialist PPI with rear-structure photos, plus cooling-system invoices.
Up: a price negotiated toward the fair-value mid-range, given a year on the market.
Up: a clean history report confirming the owner count and mileage trail.
Down: any rear subframe or trunk-floor cracking, coolant loss, or the seller refusing a PPI.
Down: a branded title, a mileage discrepancy, or undisclosed powertrain modifications found at inspection.
evidence.mission_note: A manual M54 3.0i roadster in the ideal price band is squarely the enthusiast-bridge target. Its fit depends on proving the cooling system and rear structure, because the buyer is replacing a car with a cooling failure and should not inherit another one.
evidence.rationale: The listing establishes identity reasonably well: the photographed VIN decodes as a 2001 Z3 3.0i roadster, and the photos confirm a factory manual and a well-kept black/red interior and soft top. Everything else rests on seller prose: clean title, 58,000 miles and no damage, with zero service records. The engine bay photo shows undisclosed changes, an aftermarket strut brace and what appears to be a replacement aluminium radiator, so some cooling work has likely occurred, but with no date or invoice. The two model-critical items, rear subframe/trunk-floor integrity and cooling-system history, are unaddressed. The single underside photo shows only the front/mid section, which looks clean. The $15,250 ask is slightly above the $11,754–$14,977 fair-value range, and the ad has cycled for about a year at an unchanged price. PPI access and seller cooperation are unknown, and the car is in South Carolina.
evidence.next_action: Message the seller asking for PPI permission at a Columbia-area BMW specialist, trunk-floor and rear-subframe photos, cooling-system invoices (including the radiator date), and tire DOT codes before discussing price.
